name: Caroline Diaz
life: “I still remember washing sheets for an unexpected child who stayed years.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Caroline by a small Friday habit. Caroline checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I raised her after she left. I want her to know going back doesn't cancel the years she calls me Mum.
appearance: Caroline has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Look for a long silver braid. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an old plum windbreaker with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. In conversation Caroline counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Caroline treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To keep the daughter's present home open to her.
family: Avery Lai is Caroline’s younger relative by marriage. Caroline can always ask for five minutes alone. Avery asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The fitting mirror*, Avery says, “I used it to practice asking for my old job back.”
connections: Iva Salas (foster daughter). The foster mother gives the returning adult permission to love more than one home.

reactions.situation: The father offers a letter instead of speaking
reactions.response: Caroline asks whether the daughter wants to take the letter now or leave it closed for another day.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Caroline puts distance between the frightened person and the argument and asks nearby staff for help.
